source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Power on system and mount ISO image via BMC.
2. Install Linux OS (with all packages).
3. Check OS event logs.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Os Installation should be completed successfully
2. System should be workable after reboot
3. System event log should not have error/fail/warning messages (except the message is a known event.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" -X POST https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/VirtualMedia/1/Actions/VirtualMedia.InsertMedia -d '{"Image":"http://${VIRTMEDIA_HOST:?operator must host the ISO on an HTTP server reachable by the BMC}/os.iso","Inserted":true}' -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n"; echo ---; curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/VirtualMedia/1 | jq .Image,.Inserted
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: mount a virtual-media ISO via Redfish VirtualMedia.InsertMedia, confirm the image is mounted, then proceed with the OS installation steps.
deepseek_columns.risk: STATE-CHANGING: mounts a remote ISO into the BMC CD. Approval required (R6); keep PARTIAL. ISO URL must be BMC-reachable. VirtualMedia/1 path kept per library; verify with 11/12.RestAPI before live run.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL identifies ISO mounting and BMC reachability, but a fixed Redfish path with `curl -k` and HTTP-hosted media covers only insertion. It does not validate ISO identity, transport/authentication, SUT attachment, boot selection, destructive target disk, full package installation, reboot usability, event-log acceptance or eject cleanup.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires secure endpoint/media validation, designated storage, console installation, boot control, post-install device/log comparison and mandatory eject. V3.1 further treats the source's full Linux installation—not mere mount—as the coverage objective and rejects the 10/0-minute fields as an execution deadline.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 915/2291 accepts the InsertMedia command conditionally but leaves installer interaction, storage safety, all-packages definition, known-event allowlist, boot state, endpoint discovery and cleanup unspecified.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: Earlier CIFS/NFS/HTTP/HTTPS virtual-media transport rows may validate mount paths but cannot substitute for this end-to-end Linux installation. OS-install and boot-device cases likewise do not prove BMC media insertion/ejection.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1077, Wistron-BMC-00206-V003 or 2aebe0ffa1490bc6 draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves mount, install-all-packages, reboot and log requirements; ED-34 treats image, disk, package set, endpoint and known events as Project readiness inputs; ED-35 forbids reducing the case to InsertMedia readback; ED-38 requires destructive confirmation, recovery and no automatic retry.

original_test_intent: Verify the approved BMC virtual-media path can attach a trusted Linux ISO to the correct SUT, boot it, complete the Project-defined full-package OS installation on an explicitly designated disposable target, reboot into a usable system and leave only approved known event-log entries.
original_method: Discover and validate the target firmware's virtual-media resource, securely attach an immutable verified ISO, confirm BMC transfer and host device visibility, select the media for one approved boot, perform the Project installation profile on a proven safe disk through console/automation, verify installed OS/package/device health and logs after reboot, then eject media and clear temporary boot state.
manual_activity: An engineer approves the immutable ISO, exact installation profile and target disk, reviews endpoint/boot/recovery safety and confirms the destructive install. A human may need to operate KVM/SOL/installer prompts and validate display/boot recovery. Automation can discover media resources, verify hashes/status and collect installer/OS evidence, but cannot infer a safe disk or authorize installation.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT/firmware/BIOS identity and current virtual-media, boot and host state
Vendor-supported virtual-media resource/action discovery, insert/eject semantics and transfer/connection properties
Trusted immutable ISO URL, hash/signature, OS/version/architecture and BMC-reachable authenticated transport
Exact disposable installation disk identity and proof it is not boot/EFI/mounted/swap/LVM/RAID/device-mapper or other protected data
Project OS edition, UEFI/legacy mode, partitioning, package/driver/repository manifest and unattended/manual install parameters
Approved one-time boot, power/reboot and installation window with console and recovery
Post-install OS/device/service checks and pinned event-log known-message allowlist
Required eject, override clear and final-state cleanup
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC/SEL, existing OS, installer, storage or audit logs; preserve pre-install identity and first-failure evidence.
Never guess the Redfish manager/media index, disable TLS validation, expose credentials or use an unauthenticated mutable HTTP image as the formal method.
Never guess the installation disk. Prove the exact target and protect every OS/boot/EFI/mounted/swap/LVM/RAID/device-mapper/unknown device before destructive confirmation.
Verify ISO hash/signature, target SUT and actual connected media before any boot override; an accepted InsertMedia response is not sufficient.
Obtain distinct point-of-action approval for media attach, boot/power and destructive install. Do not automatically retry download, boot, partitioning or installation.
Stop on wrong media/disk/boot path, transfer/checksum error, installer warning, device loss or unapproved logs; preserve evidence, detach safely when possible and use recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, discover the actual media resource/actions, verify secure immutable image, safe disk, installation manifest, approvals and recovery; present each state-changing/destructive boundary for confirmation.
After approval, attach once, capture complete transfer/insert/connected and host-device evidence, then pause for one-time boot/install confirmation.
Collect console/installer/package/reboot evidence and compare OS identity, devices, services and logs against Project acceptance and known-event allowlist.
Eject media, clear temporary boot state, archive raw/redacted evidence and stop without insecure TLS, guessed storage, log clear, automatic retry/reinstall or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the media endpoint/transport, immutable ISO and Project-defined `all packages` installation profile.
Verify and approve the exact disposable disk, destructive installation, boot/reboot window and recovery plan.
Review end-to-end attach/install/reboot/usability/log/cleanup evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Only partial and unsafe as a formal method: the fixed resource may be wrong, `-k` disables trust, credentials are exposed, HTTP media may be mutable, and Image/Inserted readback proves neither transfer/host visibility nor installation, disk safety, reboot or cleanup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover the vendor-supported media resource and use approved TLS/authentication to attach the verified ISO. The later executor must separately confirm safe storage and boot/install actions; no generic destructive install command is safe without Project inputs.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The power-on/mount, Linux installation with all packages, reboot usability and log Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek curl/jq proposal/risk and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not interpret zero machine time as proof the install is instantaneous or out of scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a secured end-to-end virtual-media install with resource discovery, immutable media verification, explicit safe disk, Project package profile, console evidence, post-reboot health/log checks and mandatory eject/boot cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC virtual-media implementation and dedicated SUT with disposable installation storage and recovery console.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/Redfish schema, BIOS/UEFI, ISO/OS/kernel, installer, repository/package manifest, storage/controller and console versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: BMC vendor VirtualMedia specification, Project OS deployment recipe, approved storage map, security/PKI policy and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the ambiguous endpoint, ISO, disk, packages, log allowlist and cleanup measurable while retaining full OS installation coverage.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Insert/readback alone proves only a management request; mount/host visibility does not prove boot or install; install success alone does not prove BMC transport/eject; an alternative tool does not automatically prove WebUI/API coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Media action/image, safe disk, install recipe, boot approvals, acceptance and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The workflow can destroy storage, alter boot state and install untrusted code; network media failures or leftover attachment can affect subsequent boots.

project_override_considerations: A Project may choose WebUI, Redfish or a vendor tool and a supported protocol, but must preserve the original end-to-end mount/install/reboot/log objective, record method/image/disk/reason/approval and identify uncovered interface coverage. A mount-only override is partial evidence and cannot claim this full case passed.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/boot/storage identity, protected-device map, destructive approval, Project install/package recipe and pre-test logs
Discovered media resource/action, TLS/authentication method, ISO URL/version/hash/signature and BMC reachability/transfer/connected/host-visibility evidence
One-time boot and console/installer evidence naming the exact target disk, partitioning, OS version, drivers and complete Project package result
Post-reboot OS usability, services, complete device/storage/network inventory and BMC/SEL/OS event comparison against the pinned known-event allowlist
Media eject/disconnect, boot override clear, no out-of-scope storage mutation, recovery disposition, no retry and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently require a virtual-media-based Linux installation through reboot and event-log validation. The zero machine time, open parenthesis and undefined `all packages`/known events are source-quality/readiness gaps, not competing test purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The end-to-end mount/install objective is identifiable. Project inputs can supply a trusted image, safe disk, install profile, endpoint and recovery, so execution remains pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but rejects fixed insecure insert/readback as full coverage and adds destructive disk, installation, reboot, log and eject requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on critical hybrid controls and strengthens immutable image/transport, protected-device proof, all-packages manifest and the distinction between attach, boot and install coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces command-exists sanity with an end-to-end safe installation/evidence contract.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps transport-only virtual-media cases and generic OS installation separate from this combined path.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an insecure InsertMedia response from being reported as a completed Linux installation and prevents an undefined or production disk from being overwritten while still preserving the source's full functional coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Virtual media has separate control, data and host layers: an action may be accepted while media transfer fails, and connected media may never be selected by firmware. The source then adds destructive installation and post-reboot acceptance. Therefore the evidence chain must prove immutable media, host visibility, safe boot and disk selection, installer completion, OS health/logs and detach/override cleanup; none of those later checkpoints can be inferred from API status alone.
